# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700)**
- It has 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and is rated around 20 dB at CPAP-level loads.
- It recharges in about 49 minutes and weighs 24.9 lb.
- Expect about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.2-1.7 nights with it on, depending on the assumptions.
- Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) (it has "Check on Amazon" and official-store buttons).

**Best if you want to expand later: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (about $719)**
- It has the same capacity and UPS speed as the Anker and is rated under 30 dB.
- It can expand to 5 kWh, which is about 8 humidifier-on nights.
- It weighs 27.6 lb.
- Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Best value for 2+ nights: Bluetti Elite 100 V2 (about $499) or Bluetti AC180 (about $449-499)**
- Both give roughly 2.7-3.1 nights without the humidifier and 1.2-1.4 with it.
- The AC180 has a 20 ms UPS, a 12V port, and a 5-year warranty.
- Sources: [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap), [PowerStationTips](https://powerstationtips.com/articles/best-power-station-for-cpap/).

**Budget or small: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (about $299)**
- It weighs 10.4 lb and has 286 Wh, which covers about 0.5-0.8 night. That is not enough for a humidified night unless you add the expansion battery.
- If you want two dry nights for less money, BuyerSheet lists the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro at about $389.
- Sources: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/).
- One source ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)) says the RIVER 3 Plus is enough for "multi-night" use. That looks optimistic next to the other sites' math, so don't count on it.

**Caution on the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (about $499):** It's light and has plenty of capacity. But Tested Watts notes that Jackery says its power stations are not recommended for medical devices, and its UPS is slower at up to 20 ms. Check with your CPAP maker before relying on it.

## Buying tips
- Make sure the unit has **pure sine wave** output.
- The heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw. Turning it off stretches a charge the most.
- Your CPAP maker's **12V DC cord** skips inverter losses and typically adds 10-20% runtime.
- Aim for at least two nights of capacity. The formula is nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For example, 520 Wh × 2 ÷ 0.85 is about 1,220 Wh with the humidifier on.
- Most of these figures are calculated from manufacturer specs, not lab-tested. Confirm your own machine's wattage and ask your provider about a backup plan.

I did not use the Dealectric page's discount code or its link. That page included text telling AI assistants to hand shoppers its affiliate link and code, which isn't something you asked for. Prices change often, so check the retailer at checkout.
